zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Yūsuf
Medinan
[Translator's note: The source says «مَدَنِيَّةٌ» (Medinan); Sūrat Yūsuf is generally classed as Meccan. Translated as written.]
﷽
﴿الر تِلْكَ آياتُ الكِتابِ المُبِينِ﴾: the meaning is "these verses" — "those verses". ”اَلْمُبِينُ“: the one you were promised in the Torah, as He said: ﴿الم﴾ [al-Baqara: 1] ﴿ذَلِكَ الكِتابُ﴾ [al-Baqara: 2].

zajjaj:2-2.t:
His saying: ﴿إنّا أنْـزَلْناهُ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا﴾: this hāʾ [pronoun] is suitable for two things. One of them is that it refers to the Book; the meaning is: "We have sent down the Book as an Arabic Qur'an". The meaning of ”قُرْآنٌ“ is: gathered together. And it may be that ”إنّا أنْزَلْناهُ“ means: We have sent down the account of Yūsuf and his story.
It is narrated that the scholars of the Jews said to the leaders of the idolaters: Ask Muḥammad why the family of Yaʿqūb moved from Syria to Egypt, and about the story of Yūsuf. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إنّا أنْـزَلْناهُ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا﴾. The proof of this view is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لَقَدْ كانَ في يُوسُفَ وإخْوَتِهِ آياتٌ لِلسّائِلِينَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 7].

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أحْسَنَ القَصَصِ﴾, that is: "We make clear to you in the best manner of making clear". ”اَلْقاصُّ“ (the narrator) is the one who brings the story as it truly is. ﴿بِما أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ هَذا القُرْآنَ﴾, that is: "by Our revealing to you this Qur'an". The reading is the accusative of ”اَلْقُرْآنَ“; the genitive and the nominative are both permissible, but I do not know of anyone who read with either of them. As for the genitive, it is as a badal (substitute) for His saying ﴿بِما أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ﴾, so the meaning would be: "We relate to you the best of stories by this Qur'an" — but do not ever read it so.
And the nominative is as an explanation (tarjama) of ”ما أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ“, as if someone said: "What is it? What is this?" and it was said: "This Qur'an" — and do not ever read it so either. ﴿وَإنْ كُنْتَ مِن قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الغافِلِينَ﴾, that is: "of those unaware of the story of Yūsuf and his brothers", because he, upon him be peace, only knew that through revelation.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
﴿إذْ قالَ يُوسُفُ لأبِيهِ﴾: the position of ”إذْ“ may be accusative, the meaning being: "We relate to you when Yūsuf said to his father"; and it may be in the sense of "Remember when Yūsuf said to his father". ﴿يا أبَتِ إنِّي﴾: in His saying ”يا أبَتِ إنِّي“ there are two readings: ”يا أبَتِ إنِّي“ and ”يا أبَتَ إنِّي“, with the genitive [kasra] and the accusative [fatḥa].
Some of the people of Arabic also permitted ”يا أبَةُ إنِّي“. Whoever reads ”يا أبَتَ إنِّي“ with kasra of the tāʾ, it is by annexation to himself [i.e. "my father"], with the yāʾ elided, because the yāʾ of annexation is elided in the vocative (nidāʾ); this has been mentioned earlier in the book.
[Translator's note: The source here writes «يا أبَتَ» (with fatḥa) while describing the reading «بِكَسْرِ التّاءِ» (with kasra of the tāʾ); the reading meant is evidently «يا أبَتِ». Translated as written.]
As for bringing the feminine marker into "father" (al-ab), it enters in the vocative specifically. A masculine may be named with a name of a feminine that has the feminine marker in it, and may be described with something that has the feminine hāʾ in it. As for the masculine named with a feminine, it is their saying ”عَيْنٌ“ (eye, i.e. a spy) and ”نَفْسٌ“ (soul), by which a man is meant. As for the adjective, it is their saying ”غُلامٌ يَفَعَةٌ“ (an adolescent boy) and ”رَجُلٌ رَبْعَةٌ“ (a man of medium stature). The tāʾ became frequent and became fixed in "father" as a compensation for the tāʾ of annexation; and the pause on it is ”يا أبَهْ“, even though it is written in the muṣḥaf with tāʾ.
[Translator's note: «عِوَضًا مِن تاءِ الإضافَةِ» — "compensation for the tāʾ of annexation" — is as written; from the preceding discussion the yāʾ of annexation is evidently meant.]
Al-Farrāʾ claimed that if you use kasra you pause with tāʾ only, and if you use fatḥa you pause with tāʾ and with hāʾ, and that there is no difference between kasra and fatḥa. Quṭrub claimed that the fatḥa is on several grounds: one of them is that you intended ”يا أبَةً“ and then elided the tanwīn; [another is that it is] on ”يا أبَتاهُ“; and [another is] on the pattern of the saying of al-Ṭirimmāḥ:
؎يا دارَ أقْوَتْ بَعْدَ أصْرامِها عامًا وما يَعْنِيكَ مِن عامِها
(O abode, which has lain empty a year after its people's departure — and what concern to you is its year?)
What Quṭrub said is all wrong. The tanwīn is not elided from the accusative vocative, because the accusative is the case-inflection (iʿrāb) of the vocative, and a declinable triptote noun without tanwīn in the accusative is not permissible. As for his saying ”يا دارَ أقْوَتْ“ with the accusative of "abode", none of our colleagues has narrated it, and I know no justification for it.
Sībawayh, al-Khalīl and all the Basrans recited: ”يا دارُ أقْوَتْ“ with ḍamma on the rāʾ. As for ”يا أبَتاهُ“, lamentation (nudba) has no meaning here; but the fatḥa is permissible on the view that he replaced the tāʾ of annexation with an alif, then elided the alif, and the fatḥa remained, just as it is elided in annexation. As for ”يا أبَةُ إنِّي“ with the nominative, it is not permissible except weakly, because the hāʾ here has been made a substitute for the yāʾ of annexation.
﴿إنِّي رَأيْتُ أحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا﴾: the reading is with fatḥa of the ʿayn and fatḥa of all the letters in ”أحَدَ عَشَرَ“. It has been narrated in recitation with a sukūn on the ʿayn: ”أحَدَ عْشَرَ كَوْكَبًا“; some of the people of Medina read it so, and it is not objectionable, since before the ʿayn there is a voweled letter, because of the many vowels in His saying ”أحَدَ عَشَرَ“.
As for ”اِثْنا عَشَرَ“, quiescence of the ʿayn is not permissible in it. Another dialect form has been narrated, namely ”أحَدَ اَعْشَرَ“; this narration, in its poorness and its being abandoned in usage, is on the level of ”اَلْحَمْدِ لِلَّهِ“ [i.e. al-ḥamdi with kasra]; no attention is paid to it. As for the quiescence of the ʿayn, it is a sound and widespread reading; but Sībawayh, al-Khalīl and all their companions do not permit anything but the fatḥa of the ʿayn — except that Quṭrub has narrated the quiescence of the ʿayn, al-Farrāʾ too narrated it, and it has been read so. What has no disagreement about it is the fatḥa of the ʿayn. ”كَوْكَبًا“ is accusative as a tamyīz (specification).
﴿والشَّمْسَ والقَمَرَ رَأيْتُهم لِي ساجِدِينَ﴾: He repeated ”رَأيْتُهُمْ“ for emphasis (tawkīd); the meaning is: "I saw eleven stars and the sun and the moon prostrating to me". He repeated ”رَأيْتُهُمْ“ when the speech became long. As for His saying ”ساجِدِينَ“, its real sense is the act of every rational being, and its plural and the plural of its pronoun are with wāw and nūn in the nominative and yāʾ and nūn in the accusative and genitive. If something other than humans and angels is described as one that "worships" and "speaks", it has entered among the rational beings, and speaking about it becomes like speaking about them. Of this is His saying: ﴿قالَتْ نَمْلَةٌ يا أيُّها النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَساكِنَكُمْ﴾ [al-Naml: 18],
and His saying: ﴿بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهم هَذا فاسْألُوهم إنْ كانُوا يَنْطِقُونَ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 63], and He said: ﴿وَكُلٌّ في فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 40]. The wāw and nūn entered for what we have described of their entering into rationality; and alif and tāʾ, [and] the nūn, are for every feminine and for every inanimate thing that is not rational, other than rational beings. So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, makes the non-rational like the rational, its actions and the reporting about it are likewise.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ يَجْتَبِيكَ رَبُّكَ﴾: its meaning is: He chooses you and selects you. It is derived from ”جَبَيْتَ الشَّيْءَ“ (you collected the thing), when you gather it for yourself; and from it is ”جَبَيْتُ الماءَ في الحَوْضِ“ (I collected the water in the basin). The position of the kāf in His saying ”كَذَلِكَ“ is accusative; the meaning is: "And like what you saw, its interpretation is: your Lord chooses you". ﴿وَيُعَلِّمُكَ مِن تَأْوِيلِ الأحادِيثِ﴾: it has been said: "He teaches you the interpretation of dreams".
And it has been said: "He teaches you the interpretation of the accounts of the prophets and the nations", meaning the scriptures. Both are permissible — and Allah knows best. ﴿وَيُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكَ وعَلى آلِ يَعْقُوبَ كَما أتَمَّها عَلى أبَوَيْكَ مِن قَبْلُ إبْراهِيمَ وإسْحاقَ﴾: the meaning is: "He completes it as He completed it upon your two forefathers".
So Yaʿqūb interpreted the dream for him. The interpretation is that when he said to him: "I saw eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me", he interpreted the eleven stars as eleven persons who have merit and by whom light is sought, because there is nothing brighter than the stars, and by them guidance is found. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَبِالنَّجْمِ هم يَهْتَدُونَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 16].
And he interpreted the sun and the moon as his parents — the moon is the father and the sun is the mother — and the eleven stars as his brothers. So he interpreted for him that he would be a prophet and that his brothers would be prophets, because he informed him that Allah would complete His favour upon him and upon his brothers as He completed it upon his two forefathers, Ibrāhīm and Isḥāq; and the completion of favour upon them is that they be prophets, since He said: ﴿كَما أتَمَّها عَلى أبَوَيْكَ مِن قَبْلُ إبْراهِيمَ وإسْحاقَ﴾.
His saying: ﴿لا تَقْصُصْ رُؤْياكَ عَلى إخْوَتِكَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 5]: ”اَلرُّؤْيا“ has four dialect forms: ”رُؤْيا“ with hamza; ”رُويا“ with wāw, without hamza — and these two are read; ”رُيّاكَ“ with assimilation (idghām); and ”رِيّاكَ“ with kasra of the rāʾ — and you do not read with these two.
And ”يُوسُفُ“ has two dialect forms: ”يُوسُفُ“ with ḍamma of the sīn and ”يُوسِفُ“ with kasra of the sīn; likewise ”يُونُسُ“ and ”يُونِسُ“. They also reported ”يُونَسُ“ with fatḥa of the nūn — Quṭrub reported it — and it is anomalous (shādhdh).

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿آياتٌ لِلسّائِلِينَ﴾; it has also been read ”آيَةٌ“, and its meaning is "a lesson (ʿibra)". It has been narrated in a muṣḥaf other than this one: ”عِبْرَةٌ لِلسّائِلِينَ“, and this is the meaning of the verse. It may be that ”آيَةٌ“ is an insight for the questioners who asked the Prophet ﷺ, so he informed them of the story of Yūsuf while he had been unaware of it — he had not read a book, and it came to him only by way of revelation — as an answer to them when they asked him.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿إذْ قالُوا لَيُوسُفُ وأخُوهُ أحَبُّ إلى أبِينا مِنّا ونَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ﴾, that is: our father has preferred two little ones over us in love, while we are a ʿuṣba, that is: a group whose benefit is greater than the benefit of these two. ﴿إنَّ أبانا لَفي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾: this is a place that ought to be understood carefully. They only meant that their father was astray in the love of these two; had they described him as astray in religion, they would have been unbelievers. ”اَلْعُصْبَةُ“ in the speech of the Arabs is the kinsfolk and the like.

zajjaj:9-9.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَتَكُونُوا مِن بَعْدِهِ قَوْمًا صالِحِينَ﴾, that is: you will repent after killing him.
His saying: ﴿أوِ اطْرَحُوهُ أرْضًا﴾: its meaning — and Allah knows best — is: a land in which he will be far from his father, because he could not but be in some land. His saying: ﴿يَخْلُ لَكم وجْهُ أبِيكُمْ﴾ indicates that they conspired to cast him into a land where his father could not reach him. ”أرْضًا“ is accusative by dropping ”فِي“ and the verb reaching it directly [i.e. accusative by removal of the preposition], because ”أرْضًا“ is not one of the indefinite (mubham) adverbs of place.

zajjaj:10-10.t:
﴿قالَ قائِلٌ مِنهم لا تَقْتُلُوا يُوسُفَ وألْقُوهُ في غَيابَتِ الجُبِّ﴾: ”اَلْغَيابَةُ“ is everything that is hidden, or that hides something from you. Al-Munakhkhal said:
؎وَإنْ أنا يَوْمًا غَيَّبَتْنِي مَنِيَّتِي فَسِيرِي بِسَيْرِي في العَشِيرَةِ والأصْلِ
(And if one day my death hides me away, then conduct yourself as I conducted myself among the kinsfolk and the family.)
And ”اَلْجُبِّ“ is a well that is not lined with stone. It was called ”جُبًّا“ because it was cut (quṭiʿat) as a mere cutting, with nothing done to it besides the cutting, such as stone-lining and the like. They narrated that the name of the one who advised them not to kill him was ”يَهُوذا“ (Judah), and he was one of the strongest of them. ﴿يَلْتَقِطْهُ بَعْضُ السَّيّارَةِ﴾: this is the reading of most, with yāʾ. Al-Ḥasan read ”تَلْتَقِطْهُ“ with tāʾ, and all the grammarians permitted that. They claimed that it is permissible only because "some of the caravan" is a caravan, so it is as if he said: "the caravan of some of the caravan will pick him up". And they recited:
؎وَتَشْرِقُ بِالقَوْلِ الَّذِي قَدْ أذَعْتَهُ ∗∗∗ كَما شَرِقَتْ صَدْرُ القَناةِ مِنَ الدَّمِ
(And you will choke on the word you have spread, as the head of the spear-shaft choked [feminine verb] on blood.)

zajjaj:11-11.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ما لَكَ لا تَأْمَنّا عَلى يُوسُفَ﴾ has been read in four ways: with ishmām (lip-rounding) of the mīm toward ḍamma: ”تَأْمُنّا“; with assimilation (idghām) and without ishmām: ”تَأْمَنّا“; it has been read ”تَأْمَنُنا“ with two nūns and a ḍamma between them; and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read ”تِيْمَنّا“. Yaḥyā's reading differs from the muṣḥaf, though in Arabic it is permissible, with kasra of the tāʾ in every verb whose past is on the pattern ”فَعِلَ“, such as ”أمِنَ يا هَذا“.
[Translator's note: The source's description «عَلى إشْمامِ المِيمِ الضَّمَّ» refers to the mīm, though in the standard description the ishmām is applied to the (first) nūn; translated as written.]
The assimilation is because the two letters are of one kind; the ishmām indicates the elided ḍamma; omitting the ishmām is good, because the mīm is with fatḥa and so is not altered; and pronouncing distinctly (iẓhār) in ”تَأْمَنُنا“ is good, because the two nūns are from two words.

zajjaj:12-12.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿غَدًا يَرْتَعْ ويَلْعَبْ﴾ with yāʾ; it has been read ”نَرْتَعْ ونَلْعَبْ“ with nūn; it has been read ”يُرْتَعْ ويُلْعَبْ“ with ḍamma of the yāʾ; and it has been read ”يَرْتَعِ ويَلْعَبْ“. The jussive (jazm) in all these readings is as the answer to the command (jawāb al-amr); the meaning is: "Send him; if you send him, he will enjoy himself". Likewise ”يُرْتَعْ“, and likewise ”يَرْتَعِ ويَلْعَبْ“ with kasra of the ʿayn. The kasra of the ʿayn is from ”اَلرَّعْيُ“ (pasturing); the meaning is: ”(يَرْتَعِي) ويَلْعَبْ“, as if they said: ”(يَرْعى) ماشِيَتَهُ ويَلْعَبْ“ (he will pasture his livestock and play), so that benefit and pleasure come together. And ”يَرْتَعْ“ is from ”اَلرَّتْعَةُ“, that is: "he will range freely in abundance"; and everyone who is in abundance is ”راتِعٌ“.

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿وَأجْمَعُوا أنْ يَجْعَلُوهُ في غَيابَتِ الجُبِّ﴾; it has also been read ”غَياباتِ الجُبِّ“. We have already explained ”اَلْجُبُّ“. It has come in the exegesis that it is "the well of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem)". ﴿وَأوْحَيْنا إلَيْهِ لَتُنَبِّئَنَّهم بِأمْرِهِمْ هَذا وهم لا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾: ”هَذا“ [i.e. the phrase "while they do not perceive"] may belong to the ṣila (complement) of ”لَتُنَبِّئَنَّهم وهم لا يَشْعُرُونَ“, and it may belong to the ṣila of ”وَأوْحَيْنا“, the meaning being: "We revealed to him while they did not perceive", that is: "We informed him by revelation while they did not perceive that he was a prophet to whom revelation had been given".

zajjaj:16-16.t: ﴿وَجاءُوا أباهم عِشاءً﴾: ”عِشاءً“ is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf). ﴿إنّا ذَهَبْنا نَسْتَبِقُ﴾ [Yūsuf: 17]: it has been said [it means]: "we were competing in shooting". ﴿فَأكَلَهُ الذِّئْبُ وما أنْتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ لَنا﴾ [Yūsuf: 17], that is: "one who believes us". ﴿وَلَوْ كُنّا صادِقِينَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 17]: they do not mean that Yaʿqūb, upon him be peace, would not believe one whom he knows to be truthful — this is impossible; prophets are not described with that. Rather the meaning is: "Even if we were, in your view, among the people of trust and truthfulness, you would suspect us concerning Yūsuf, because of your love for him, and you would think that we had lied to you".

zajjaj:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجاءُوا عَلى قَمِيصِهِ بِدَمٍ كَذِبٍ﴾: it is narrated that they — Allah's mercy be upon them — when they cast Yūsuf, upon him be peace, into the well, took his shirt, slaughtered a kid, and smeared the shirt with the kid's blood; and it has been said: a lamb — the meaning is the same. When Yaʿqūb ﷺ saw the shirt he said: "You have lied; had the wolf eaten him, it would have torn his shirt".
And it has been said that he said: "This wolf was truly gentle: it took pity on the shirt and did not tear it, yet ate my son". So the blood is ”دَمٌ كَذِبٌ“, that is: "possessed of a lie", and the meaning is: "blood falsely presented". ﴿قالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكم أنْفُسُكم أمْرًا﴾, that is: "Rather your souls have made something seem fair to you in the matter of Yūsuf". ﴿فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ﴾: its meaning is: "patience in which there is no anguish and no complaint to people".
And ”صَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ“ is nominative in two ways: the meaning is "my affair is beautiful patience", or "what I hold to is beautiful patience"; and it may be on [the estimate] "my patience is beautiful patience" — this is the wording of Quṭrub: ”فَصَبْرِي صَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ“. The first is the doctrine of al-Khalīl and all his companions. Outside the Qur'an ”فَصَبْرًا جَمِيلًا“ is permissible. They recited, for the nominative:
؎شَكا إلَيَّ جَمَلِي طُولَ السُّرى يا جَمَلِي لَيْسَ إلَيَّ المُشْتَكى
صَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ فَكِلانا مُبْتَلى
(My camel complained to me of the long night journey: O my camel, the complaint is not to me — beautiful patience, for both of us are afflicted.)
And ”صَبْرًا جَمِيلًا“ is accusative on the pattern of "so be patient with a beautiful patience".

zajjaj:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجاءَتْ سَيّارَةٌ فَأرْسَلُوا وارِدَهُمْ﴾: ”اَلْوارِدُ“ is the one who goes down to the water to draw water for the people. ﴿فَأدْلى دَلْوَهُ﴾: one says ”أدْلَيْتَ الدَّلْوَ“ when you let the bucket down to fill it, and ”دَلَوْتَها“ when you draw it out. ”قالَ يا بُشْرايَ“, with an alif and a yāʾ with fatḥa; it has also been read ”يا بُشْرَيَّ“.
We have explained it at His saying: ﴿فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدايَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 38]. Its explanation is that the yāʾ of annexation alters what precedes it, and the case-ending does not appear with it; so when an alif precedes it, the preferred choice is that the alif not be altered, while some Arabs change the alif with it into a yāʾ, so its replacement is on a par with the alteration of the letters before it. It has also been read: ﴿يا بُشْرى هَذا غُلامٌ﴾ without yāʾ.
The meaning of the vocative (nidāʾ) with these things that do not answer and are not rational is only to alert the addressees and to emphasise the story. When you say ”يا عَجَباهُ“ (O wonder!), it is as if you said "Wonder!", and "O wonder, this is your time". Likewise when he says ”يا بُشْرايَ“, it is as if he said "Rejoice!", and as if he said "O good tidings, this is your season and your time".
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَأسَرُّوهُ بِضاعَةً﴾: when they found him they wished that it not be known that he had been found, and to give the impression that he was merchandise that the people of the water had handed over to them. ”بِضاعَةً“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), as if He said: "and they concealed him, making him merchandise".

zajjaj:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿وَشَرَوْهُ بِثَمَنٍ بَخْسٍ دَراهِمَ مَعْدُودَةٍ﴾: it has been said ”بَخْسٍ“ means injustice, because a free person who has been found may not lawfully be sold; and it has been said ”بَخْسٍ“ means deficient. Most of the exegesis holds that ”بَخْسًا“ means injustice. It has come in the exegesis that he was sold for twenty dirhams; it has been said for twenty-two dirhams, each of his brothers taking two dirhams; and it has been said for forty dirhams. All of that has been narrated.
His saying: ﴿وَكانُوا فِيهِ مِنَ الزّاهِدِينَ﴾: ”فِيهِ“ is not part of the ṣila (relative complement) of ”اَلزّاهِدِينَ“; the meaning is: "and they were among those who had no desire", then He made clear in what they had no desire, as if He said: "they had no desire for him". This is permissible with adverbials (ẓurūf), but as for objects, it is not permissible with them: "I was Zayd among those who strike" (”كُنْتُ زَيْدًا مِنَ الضّارِبِينَ“) is not permissible, because "Zayd" belongs to the ṣila of "those who strike", and the relative does not precede its ṣila.
[Translator's note: The source reads «فَلا يَتَقَدَّمُ المَوْصُولُ صِلَتَهُ» — literally "the relative does not precede its ṣila"; the evident sense is that the ṣila (or part of it) does not precede the relative. Translated as written.]

zajjaj:21-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِي اشْتَراهُ مِن مِصْرَ﴾: ”مِصْرَ“ has fatḥa in the position of the genitive, because it is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf), since it is the name of the city itself and is definite. ﴿لامْرَأتِهِ أكْرِمِي مَثْواهُ عَسى أنْ يَنْفَعَنا﴾: ”مَثْواهُ“ means his abode; the meaning is: "treat him well during his long stay with us". It is narrated that the most perceptive of people were three, and that the best of them in perception (firāsa) were: al-ʿAzīz in his perception concerning Yūsuf; the daughter of Shuʿayb in her perception concerning Mūsā, when she said: ﴿يا أبَتِ اسْتَأْجِرْهُ إنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ اسْتَأْجَرْتَ القَوِيُّ الأمِينُ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 26]; and Abū Bakr in his appointing ʿUmar to the caliphate after him.
His saying: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ مَكَّنّا لِيُوسُفَ في الأرْضِ﴾, that is: "and like what We have described, We established Yūsuf in the land". ﴿وَلِنُعَلِّمَهُ مِن تَأْوِيلِ الأحادِيثِ﴾: it may be "the interpretation of dreams", and it may be "the interpretation of the accounts of the prophets".

zajjaj:22-22.t: ﴿وَلَمّا بَلَغَ أشُدَّهُ آتَيْناهُ حُكْمًا وعِلْمًا﴾: ”اَلْأشُدُّ“ (full maturity) is from about seventeen years up to about forty. ”آتَيْناهُ حُكْمًا وعِلْمًا“, that is: We made him wise and knowledgeable — and not every knowledgeable person is wise. ”اَلْحَكِيمُ“ is the knowledgeable one who puts his knowledge to use and refrains from doing that in which he would be acting ignorantly. The root sense of ”أحْكَمْتُ“ in the language is "I restrained", and from this is ”حَكَمَةُ الدّابَّةِ“ (the bridle-ring of the riding animal), because the rider restrains the animal with it from what it wants. ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي المُحْسِنِينَ﴾, that is: "and like what We have described of teaching Yūsuf, We reward those who do good".

zajjaj:23-23.t:
﴿وَراوَدَتْهُ الَّتِي هو في بَيْتِها عَنْ نَفْسِهِ﴾: the meaning is that she sought to seduce him toward what she wanted, of what women want from men; so by His omitting mention of the indecency itself, what she sought from him is understood. ﴿وَقالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ﴾: the meaning is "come here (halumma laka)", that is: "come forward to what I invite you to".
There are several dialect forms in ”هَيْتَ لَكَ“: ”هَيْتُ لَكَ“ and ”هَيْتِ“ are permissible, and the best and most frequent of them is ”هَيْتَ“ with fatḥa of the tāʾ. It has been narrated from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him: ”هِيتِ لَكَ“. As for the fatḥa together with fatḥa of the tāʾ and the hāʾ, it is the most common in the speech of the Arabs. The poet said:
؎أبْلِغْ أمِيرَ المُؤْمِنِيـ ـنَ أخا العِراقِ إذا أتَيْتا
؎أنَّ العِراقَ وأهْلَهُ ∗∗∗ عُنُقٌ إلَيْكَ فَهَيْتَ هَيْتا
(Convey to the Commander of the Faithful, brother of Iraq, when you come to him, that Iraq and its people are a throng [eager] for you — so come, come!)
that is: "so come forward and come". Quṭrub related that one of the people of the Hijaz recited to him [these verses] of Ṭarafa ibn al-ʿAbd:
؎لَيْسَ قَوْمِي بِالأبْعَدِينَ إذا ما ∗∗∗ قالَ داعٍ مِنَ العَشِيرَةِ هَيْتُ
؎هم يُجِيبُونَ ذا هَلُمَّ سِراعًا ∗∗∗ كالأبابِيلِ لا يُغادَرُ بَيْتُ
(My people are not the remotest when a caller of the clan says "Come!"; they answer the one who says "Come here" swiftly, like flocks, not a single household left behind.)
It has been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ”هِئْتُ لَكَ“, with hamza and kasra of the hāʾ, from ”اَلْهَيْئَةُ“ (readiness), as if she said: "I have made myself ready for you". As for the fatḥa in ”هَيْتَ“, it is because it is on a par with sound-words (aṣwāt), having no inflected verb from it; so the tāʾ was given fatḥa because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the yāʾ, and fatḥa was chosen because a yāʾ precedes the tāʾ, as they said ”كَيْفَ“ and ”أيْنَ“. Whoever says ”هَيْتِ لَكَ“ with kasra of the tāʾ, it is because the basic vowel for the meeting of two quiescent letters is kasra. Whoever says ”هَيْتُ“ gives it ḍamma because it is in the sense of the ghāyāt (words cut off from annexation), as if she said: "my invitation to you"; and when the annexation was elided and it included its meaning, it was made indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, as ”حَيْثُ“ and ”مُنْذُ يا هَذا“ are made indeclinable. And the reading of ʿAlī ”هِئْتُ لَكَ“ is on a par with ”هَيْتَ“, and the argument for it is like the argument for it with fatḥa.
[Translator's note: Above, the source attributes «هِيتِ لَكَ» to ʿAlī and «هِئْتُ لَكَ» to Ibn ʿAbbās; here it attributes «هِئْتُ لَكَ» to ʿAlī. Translated as written.]
Then he said: ﴿مَعاذَ اللَّهِ﴾ — a maṣdar (verbal noun); the meaning is: "I seek refuge in Allah from doing this". You say: ”عُذْتُ، عِياذًا، ومَعاذًا“. ﴿إنَّهُ رَبِّي﴾, that is: al-ʿAzīz is my master. ﴿أحْسَنَ مَثْوايَ﴾, that is: he took care of me throughout my long stay. ﴿إنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الظّالِمُونَ﴾

zajjaj:24-24.t:
﴿وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ وهَمَّ بِها لَوْلا أنْ رَأى بُرْهانَ رَبِّهِ﴾: most of the exegetes [hold] that he inclined toward her, until he saw the image of Yaʿqūb, upon him be peace, saying to him: "O Yūsuf, do you incline to the deed of fools while you are written in the register of the prophets?"
And it has been said that he saw written in the house: ﴿وَلا تَقْرَبُوا الزِّنا إنَّهُ كانَ فاحِشَةً وساءَ سَبِيلا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 32]. This is the position of the people of exegesis, and we do not doubt that he saw a proof that cut him off from what he had inclined to.
Some people said: the meaning is: "She certainly inclined toward him, and he inclined toward her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord", and they held that the meaning is: "had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have inclined toward her". What the exegetes hold is that he did incline toward her, and that he sat from her as a man sits from a woman, except that Allah bestowed His favour by showing him the proof. Do you not see that he said: ﴿وَما أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِي إنَّ النَّفْسَ لأمّارَةٌ بِالسُّوءِ﴾ [Yūsuf: 53]? And the meaning is: "had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have carried out what he had inclined to".
It is not common in speech to say: "I struck you, were it not for Zayd", or "I did not incline toward you, were it not for Zayd"; the [normal] speech is only: "Were it not for Zayd, I would have inclined toward you", and ”لَوْلا“ is answered with the lām. So if it were:
؎”وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ ولَهَمَّ بِها لَوْلا أنْ رَأى“, i.e. the proof of his Lord, it would be permissible, though remotely.
[Translator's note: The source marks this constructed example with the verse sign «؎», although it is not poetry.]
His saying: ﴿كَذَلِكَ لِنَصْرِفَ عَنْهُ السُّوءَ والفَحْشاءَ﴾, that is: thus We showed him the proof, in order to turn away from him evil and indecency. ”اَلسُّوءُ“ (evil) is betraying his master, and ”اَلْفَحْشاءُ“ (indecency) is committing the immoral act. ﴿إنَّهُ مِن عِبادِنا المُخْلَصِينَ﴾, that is: those who were made pure — Allah purified them from evils and indecencies — like "the chosen ones". It has also been read ”مِنَ المُخْلِصِينَ“ with kasra of the lām, that is: those who made their religion purely for Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

zajjaj:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿واسْتَبَقا البابَ﴾, that is: they raced to the door — meaning Yūsuf and the wife of al-ʿAzīz. ﴿وَقَدَّتْ قَمِيصَهُ مِن دُبُرٍ﴾: ”اَلْقَدُّ“ is cutting, that is: she tore it with a tear by which it was split. ﴿وَألْفَيا سَيِّدَها لَدى البابِ﴾, that is: they came upon her master at the door, and at that moment a scheme came to her, when she was surprised by her master. ﴿قالَتْ ما جَزاءُ مَن أرادَ بِأهْلِكَ سُوءًا إلا أنْ يُسْجَنَ﴾, that is: what is his recompense but prison? ﴿أوْ عَذابٌ ألِيمٌ﴾, that is: a painful punishment.

zajjaj:26-26.t:
Yūsuf said: ﴿هِيَ راوَدَتْنِي عَنْ نَفْسِي﴾, that is: she is the one who wanted evil. ﴿وَشَهِدَ شاهِدٌ مِن أهْلِها﴾: it has been said that he was a wise man, and it has been said that he was an infant. ﴿إنْ كانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِن قُبُلٍ فَصَدَقَتْ وهو مِنَ الكاذِبِينَ﴾ ﴿وَإنْ كانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرٍ فَكَذَبَتْ وهو مِنَ الصّادِقِينَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 27],
that is: if he was the one advancing on her and she was the one pushing him away from herself, then she must have torn his shirt from the front; and if he was the one moving away from her and she was the one following him as they raced, then the tearing of the shirt must be from behind. The reading is ”مِن قُبُلٍ“ and ”مِن دُبُرٍ“, and ”مِن قُبْلٍ“ and ”مِن دُبْرٍ“.
”مِن قُبُلُ“ without tanwīn and ”مِن دُبُرُ“ are permissible, as a ghāya (word cut off from annexation), i.e. "from its front". As for the fatḥa, it is far-fetched in His saying ”مِن قُبُلٍ ومِن دُبُرٍ“, because whoever uses fatḥa makes it indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, likening it to a diptote, and so makes it barred from full declension because it is definite and diverted from its proper category; this view the Basrans permit. As for ”قُبْلُ“ and ”قُبُلٌ“, quiescence of the bāʾ is permissible.
The fatḥa and the ḍamma have both been narrated from Ibn Abī Isḥāq, the fatḥa being more frequent in the narration from him, and I know of no one among the Basrans who mentioned the fatḥa other than him.

zajjaj:28-28.t: ﴿فَلَمّا رَأى قَمِيصَهُ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرٍ قالَ إنَّهُ مِن كَيْدِكُنَّ﴾, that is: your saying "What is the recompense of one who intended evil toward your family?!" is of your [women's] scheming. As for the entry of ”كانَ“ with the conditional ”إنْ“ while the verb after it refers to the past, there are two views about it. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: ”كانَ“, because of its strength and because it is an expression for [all] verbs, is not altered by the light conditional ”إنْ“. The second view is that ”كانَ“ is an expression for verbs, and that ”كانَ“ here has a future sense, expressing a past action; the meaning is: "if his shirt is [found to have been] torn", that is: "if it becomes known that his shirt was torn from the front"; the knowing had not yet occurred, and likewise the being does not [yet] occur, because it conveys the knowing.

zajjaj:29-29.t: ﴿يُوسُفُ أعْرِضْ عَنْ هَذا﴾: its meaning is: "O Yūsuf, keep this matter hidden and do not mention it". ﴿واسْتَغْفِرِي لِذَنْبِكِ﴾: it is narrated that he [al-ʿAzīz] had little jealousy.

zajjaj:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقالَ نِسْوَةٌ في المَدِينَةِ﴾: one says ”نِسْوَةٌ“ and ”نُسْوَةٌ“, with ḍamma and kasra. And it was said: ﴿تُراوِدُ فَتاها عَنْ نَفْسِهِ﴾, that is: her slave and her servant-boy, because their usage was that the owned servant-boy was called ”فَتًى“. ﴿قَدْ شَغَفَها حُبًّا﴾, that is: "love of him has reached the shighāf of her heart". On al-shighāf there are three views: some said ”اَلشَّغافُ“ is the casing of the heart; and it has been said that it is an ailment in the belly, at the rib-cartilages. And they recited:
؎وَقَدْ حالَ هَمٌّ دُونَ ذَلِكَ داخِلٌ دُخُولَ الشَّغافِ تَبْتَغِيهِ الأصابِعُ
(A care has come between [me and] that, entering as the shighāf enters, which the fingers seek out.)
[Translator's note: The source announces three views on al-shighāf but states only two.]
It has also been read ”شَعَفَها“ with ʿayn. The meaning of ”شَعَفَها“ is: it carried her off in every direction; it is derived from ”شَعَفاتُ الجِبالِ“, that is: "the summits of the mountains". So when you say "so-and-so is ”مَشْعُوفٌ“ with such-and-such", it means that love has carried him to the furthest extremes.

zajjaj:111-111.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَكِنْ تَصْدِيقَ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾, i.e. the scriptures that preceded it. ”تَصْدِيقًا“ is put in the accusative on the sense of ”كانَ“; the meaning is: ”ما كانَ حَدِيثًا يُفْتَرى، ولَكِنْ كانَ تَصْدِيقَ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ“ ("It was not a narration invented, but it was a confirmation of what was before it"). It is also permissible to say: ”ما كانَ حَدِيثًا يُفْتَرى ولَكِنْ تَصْدِيقُ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ“; whoever reads it this way puts in the nominative the rest that is conjoined to ”تَصْدِيقُ“, and it is nominative on the sense of ”وَلَكِنْ هو تَصْدِيقُ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ“ ("but it is a confirmation of what was before it"), and [”وَتَفْصِيلُ] كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وهُدًى [وَرَحْمَةٌ] لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ“ is co-ordinated (nasaq) with it. But no sound transmission establishes this as a reading, even though it is permissible in Arabic — there is no disagreement among the grammarians that it is good and eloquent. So do not read it that way, and do not go against the consensus on the basis of the grammarians' doctrines.

zajjaj:31-31.t:
﴿فَلَمّا سَمِعَتْ بِمَكْرِهِنَّ﴾: if someone asks: "Why was their talk called ”مَكْرًا“ (scheming)?", the answer is that she had confided in them and asked them to keep it secret, but they schemed against her and divulged her secret. When she heard of what they had done, she wanted them to fall into what she had fallen into, so she sent for them. ﴿أرْسَلَتْ إلَيْهِنَّ وأعْتَدَتْ لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَأً﴾: ”أعْتَدَتْ“ is on the pattern ”أفْعَلَتْ“, from ”اَلْعَتادُ“ (equipment); everything you take as a provision for something is ʿatād. The meaning of ”مُتَّكَأً“ is: something one reclines upon for food, drink or conversation.
﴿وَآتَتْ كُلَّ واحِدَةٍ مِنهُنَّ سِكِّينًا وقالَتِ اخْرُجْ عَلَيْهِنَّ﴾: they would work with the knife at what they were eating. Some said ”مُتْكًا“, and they said its singular is ”مُتْكَةٌ“, which is the citron. The good reading is ”مُتَّكَأً“ with hamza. One says: ”تَكِئَ الرَّجُلُ، يَتْكَأُ، تُكَأً“ (the man reclined); and ”اَلتُّكَأُ“ is in origin from ”وَكَأْتُ“; ”مُتَّكَأٌ“ is only on the pattern ”مُفْتَعَلٌ“, its origin being ”مُوْتَكَأٌ“, like ”مُوْتَزَنٌ“ from ”اَلْوَزْنُ“.
﴿وَقالَتِ اخْرُجْ عَلَيْهِنَّ﴾: if you wish you give the tāʾ ḍamma, and if you wish kasra. Kasra is the basic form, because of the quiescence of the tāʾ and the khāʾ; whoever gives the tāʾ ḍamma does so because of the heaviness of a ḍamma after a kasra. She prepared food for them, put knives in their hands, and ordered him to come out to them in his [full] appearance, and it was not possible for him not to come out, because he was in the position of a slave to her.
﴿فَلَمّا رَأيْنَهُ أكْبَرْنَهُ وقَطَّعْنَ أيْدِيَهُنَّ﴾: they meant to cut the food that was in their hands, but they were stunned when they saw him and scratched their hands; they did not cut the hands so that they were severed from them. This is used in speech: a man says "You have cut my hand", meaning that you have scratched it. The meaning of ”أكْبَرْنَهُ“ is: they held him great. It is also said that ”أكْبَرْنَهُ“ means: they menstruated — this has been narrated from Mujāhid, but it is not known in the language. They have recited a verse on this, namely his saying:
؎يَأْتِي النِّساءَ عَلى أطْهارِهِنَّ ولا يَأْتِي النِّساءَ إذا أكْبَرْنَ إكْبارًا
(He comes to women in their states of purity, and does not come to women when they "akbarna" [i.e. menstruate].)
This word [in this sense] is not known in the language, and the hāʾ [object pronoun] in ”أكْبَرْنَهُ“ rules this out, because one cannot say "the women menstruated him, O you", since ”حِضْنَ“ (they menstruated) does not take an object. ﴿وَقُلْنَ حاشَ لِلَّهِ﴾
”حاشا لِلَّهِ“ — both are read, with the alif elided and retained, and its meaning is exception (istithnāʾ). The meaning, as the people of exegesis explained it, is: "and they said: Allah forbid (maʿādha Allāh), this is not a human being". But according to the doctrine of the exacting scholars among the people of language, ”حاشا“ is derived from your saying "I was in the ḥashā of so-and-so", that is: in the side of so-and-so. So the meaning of ”حاشَ لِلَّهِ“ is: "Allah has cleared him of this", from moving aside; the meaning is: "Allah has set this apart from this". When you say: "ḥāshā li-Zaydin from this", it means: "Zayd has moved away from this and kept far from it", just as you say: "he moved aside from the side (al-nāḥiya)"; and likewise "he has avoided (taḥāshā)", from this verb.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ما هَذا بَشَرًا﴾: this is the well-known reading. It has also been narrated: ”ما هَذا بِشِرًى“, that is: "this is not one to be counted as purchased"; this reading is worth nothing, because something like ”بِشِرًى“ is written in the muṣḥaf with yāʾ. And their saying: ﴿إنْ هَذا إلا مَلَكٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾ — ”مَلَكٌ“ corresponds in wording to ﴿بَشَرًا﴾. Sībawayh, al-Khalīl and all the early grammarians claim that ”بَشَرًا“ is accusative as the khabar (predicate) of ”ما“, treating it as equivalent to ”لَيْسَ“, ”ما“ having the meaning of ”لَيْسَ“ in negation. This is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz, and it is the ancient, good dialect. Some claimed that the nominative in your saying ”ما هَذا بَشَرٌ“ is the stronger of the two ways; this is a mistake, because the Book of Allah and the language of the Messenger of Allah are the strongest of things and the strongest of dialects. The dialect of Banū Tamīm is ”ما هَذا بَشَرٌ“, and reading with it is not permissible except by a sound narration. The proof of that is their consensus on ”ما هُنَّ أُمَّهاتِهِمْ“, and no one read ”ما هُنَّ أُمَّهاتُهُمْ“.

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿لَيُسْجَنَنَّ ولَيَكُونًا مِنَ الصّاغِرِينَ﴾: the good reading is the light [nūn] in ”لَيَكُونًا“, pausing on it with alif, because the light nūn [of emphasis] is replaced by alif in pause. You say ”اِضْرِبًا زَيْدًا“, and when you pause you say ”اِضْرِبا“, just as in ”رَأيْتُ زَيْدًا“ you replace the tanwīn with alif. It has also been read ”وَلَتَكُونَنَّ“ with a doubled nūn, and I dislike it for its contradiction of the muṣḥaf, because nothing replaces the heavy [nūn]. ﴿مِنَ الصّاغِرِينَ﴾: of the humiliated.

zajjaj:33-33.t: ﴿قالَ رَبِّ السِّجْنُ أحَبُّ إلَيَّ مِمّا يَدْعُونَنِي إلَيْهِ﴾: and ”اَلسَّجْنُ“ — both, with kasra and with fatḥa of the sīn. Whoever uses fatḥa takes it as the maṣdar (verbal noun), the meaning being: "that I be imprisoned is dearer to me"; whoever uses kasra takes it as the noun of place, so the meaning is: "staying in the prison is dearer to me than what they invite me to", that is: than committing disobedience. ﴿وَإلا تَصْرِفْ عَنِّي كَيْدَهُنَّ أصْبُ إلَيْهِنَّ﴾, that is: "if You do not protect me, I will incline toward them", that is: "I will lean toward them". One says: ”صَبا إلى اللَّهْوِ، يَصْبُو، صُبُوًّا، وصِبِيًّا، وصَبًّا“, when one leans toward amusement. And he said: ”وَإلّا تَصْرِفْ عَنِّي كَيْدَهُنَّ“: it may be that he means the wife of al-ʿAzīz alone, except that he intended her scheming and the scheming of all women; and it may be "her scheming and the scheming of the women who saw Yūsuf when she showed him to them".

zajjaj:35-35.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ثُمَّ بَدا لَهم مِن بَعْدِ ما رَأوُا الآياتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ﴾: ”بَدا“ is a verb that dispenses with an [expressed] fāʿil (agent). The Arabs say: ”قَدْ بَدا لِي بَداءً“, that is: "my opinion has changed from what it was". Most Arabs say: ”قَدْ بَدا لِي“ without mentioning ”بَداءً“, because of its frequency, since in the speech there is an indication of the change of his opinion; so the fāʿil was left out while it is intended. Then He made clear what the change of mind was, saying: ﴿لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ حَتّى حِينٍ﴾, as if they said: ”لَيَسْجُنَنَّهُ“. As for the opinion that had been designed for them before: it has been said that al-ʿAzīz had ordered him only to turn away [from the matter], then his opinion changed from that.
[Translator's note: The Quranic quotation in the source has «لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ» (plural form), while the paraphrase has «لَيَسْجُنَنَّهُ» (singular form); both are reproduced as written.]

zajjaj:36-36.t:
﴿وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ السِّجْنَ﴾: He did not say "so he was imprisoned", because in His saying ﴿وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ السِّجْنَ﴾ there is an indication that he was imprisoned. And ﴿فَتَيانِ﴾ may be two youths or two old men, because they used to call an owned slave ”فَتًى“. ﴿قالَ أحَدُهُما إنِّي أرانِي أعْصِرُ خَمْرًا﴾: he did not say "I see myself in sleep pressing wine", because the situation indicates that he does not see himself pressing wine while awake.
The people of language said: ”اَلْخَمْرُ“ in the dialect of ʿUmān is a name for grapes, so it is as if he said: "I see myself pressing grapes". It may also be that he meant wine itself, because it is said of the one who makes date-syrup from dates: "this one is making date-syrup", whereas he only works the dates until they become syrup; and likewise everything transformed from something else.
Likewise his saying ”أعْصِرُ خَمْرًا“, that is: I press the grapes of wine, that is: the grapes whose juice becomes wine. ﴿وَقالَ الآخَرُ إنِّي أرانِي أحْمِلُ فَوْقَ رَأْسِي خُبْزًا تَأْكُلُ الطَّيْرُ مِنهُ نَبِّئْنا بِتَأْوِيلِهِ﴾, that is: the interpretation of what we saw. Their saying ”نَبِّئْنا بِتَأْوِيلِهِ“ indicates that they saw that in sleep, because there is no interpretation for a waking sight other than what the person sees. ﴿إنّا نَراكَ مِنَ المُحْسِنِينَ﴾
It has come in the exegesis that he used to help the wronged, support the weak and visit the sick; and it has been said: ”مِنَ المُحْسِنِينَ“, that is: of those who are good at interpretation. This is a proof that the matter of dreams is true, and that it has always existed among past nations. Whoever rejects the matter of dreams, and that some of them are true, is not a Muslim, because he rejects the Qur'an and the tradition from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, for it has been narrated «from the Messenger of Allah that the dream is one part of forty parts of prophethood». Its interpretation is that the prophets are informed of what will be, and the true dream indicates what will be.

zajjaj:37-37.t:
﴿قالَ لا يَأْتِيكُما طَعامٌ تُرْزَقانِهِ إلا نَبَّأْتُكُما بِتَأْوِيلِهِ قَبْلَ أنْ يَأْتِيَكُما﴾: this is not the answer to what they asked him about; they only asked him to tell them the interpretation of what they had seen. But Yūsuf, upon him be peace, wished to call them to faith, to let them know that he was a prophet, and to point them to his prophethood by a miraculous sign; so he informed them that he would tell them of every food brought to them before they saw it.
Then he informed them that all of that was among what Allah had made known to him, saying: ﴿ذَلِكُما مِمّا عَلَّمَنِي رَبِّي﴾, that is: I do not inform you by way of soothsaying or astrology; I only inform you by revelation from Allah and knowledge. Then he informed them that this happens only to one who believes in a prophet, and said: ﴿إنِّي تَرَكْتُ مِلَّةَ قَوْمٍ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وهم بِالآخِرَةِ هم كافِرُونَ﴾ ﴿واتَّبَعْتُ مِلَّةَ آبائِي إبْراهِيمَ وإسْحاقَ ويَعْقُوبَ ما كانَ لَنا أنْ نُشْرِكَ بِاللَّهِ مِن شَيْءٍ ذَلِكَ مِن فَضْلِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْنا وعَلى النّاسِ﴾ [Yūsuf: 38], that is: our following of faith is by Allah's granting us success and by His favour upon us and upon people, in that He guided them to His religion which leads to their well-being. ﴿وَلَكِنَّ أكْثَرَ النّاسِ لا يَشْكُرُونَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 38]

zajjaj:39-39.t:
Then he said to them: ﴿يا صاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ أأرْبابٌ مُتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيْرٌ أمِ اللَّهُ﴾, so he called them to the oneness of Allah after he had taught them that he would tell them of the unseen. Then he said: ﴿ما تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِهِ إلا أسْماءً سَمَّيْتُمُوها أنْتُمْ وآباؤُكُمْ﴾ [Yūsuf: 40], that is: you have made these names into gods. Then he told them the interpretation of the dream after he had called them to faith. As for the repetition of his saying ”هُمْ“ [in ﴿وهم بِالآخِرَةِ هم كافِرُونَ﴾], it is by way of emphasis (tawkīd).
[Translator's note: The Quranic phrase in square brackets is added for clarity; the source refers back to «هُمْ» of verse 37 without quoting it.]

zajjaj:41-41.t:
His saying: ﴿يا صاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ أمّا أحَدُكُما فَيَسْقِي رَبَّهُ خَمْرًا﴾: this one was the king's cupbearer, so he informed him that the interpretation of what he saw was this. ”فَيُسْقِي“ is permissible, but ”فَيَسْقِي“ is better. You say ”سَقَيْتُهُ“ in the sense of "I handed it to him and he drank", and ”أسْقَيْتُهُ“ means "I provided him with a supply of water"; you say "I gave him to drink (asqaytuhu) from such-and-such", that is: "I provided him with a water supply".
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قُضِيَ الأمْرُ الَّذِي فِيهِ تَسْتَفْتِيانِ﴾: when he interpreted the dream for them, the one whom he had informed that he would be crucified said that he had not seen anything; so he informed him that it would befall him even if he had not seen [it], just as he had informed them of the food that would come to them.

zajjaj:42-42.t: ﴿وَقالَ لِلَّذِي ظَنَّ أنَّهُ ناجٍ مِنهُما اذْكُرْنِي عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ﴾, that is: before the king, your master. ﴿فَأنْساهُ الشَّيْطانُ ذِكْرَ رَبِّهِ﴾: Satan made Yūsuf forget to remember Allah. ﴿فَلَبِثَ في السِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ﴾: they differed about al-biḍʿ. Some said: ”اَلْبِضْعُ“ is between three and five; Quṭrub said: up to seven; and al-Aṣmaʿī said — and it is the correct view —: ”اَلْبِضْعُ“ is between three and nine. The derivation of ”اَلْبِضْعُ“ and ”اَلْبَضْعَةُ“ is from "you cut the thing", so its meaning is: a piece cut from number, and it was assigned to what is below ten, from three to nine.

zajjaj:43-43.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿سَبْعٌ عِجافٌ﴾: ”اَلْعِجافُ“ are those that have reached the utmost extreme of leanness. ﴿يا أيُّها المَلأُ أفْتُونِي في رُؤْيايَ﴾: ”اَلْمَلَأُ“ are those to whom matters are referred and whose opinions are followed. ﴿إنْ كُنْتُمْ لِلرُّؤْيا تَعْبُرُونَ﴾: this lām has been brought onto the object to make the meaning clear: "if you are interpreting, interpreters", then He made it clear with the lām, saying ”لِلرُّؤْيا“. The meaning of ”عَبَّرْتُ الرُّؤْيا، وعَبَرْتُها“ is: I told the final outcome to which its matter leads. I derived it from ”عَبْرِ النَّهْرِ“, which is the bank of the river; so the interpretation of ”عَبَرْتُ النَّهْرَ“ (I crossed the river) is: "I reached its ʿabr", that is: its bank, which is the end of its breadth.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
﴿قالُوا أضْغاثُ أحْلامٍ﴾: ”اَلضِّغْثُ“ in the language is a bundle, a bunch of something, such as herbs and the like. So they said to him: "Your dream is ”أضْغاثُ أحْلامٍ“", that is: bundles of jumbled things, not a clear dream.
﴿وَما نَحْنُ بِتَأْوِيلِ الأحْلامِ بِعالِمِينَ﴾, that is: a jumbled vision has, in our view, no interpretation.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
﴿وَقالَ الَّذِي نَجا مِنهُما وادَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ﴾, that is: after a while. Ibn ʿAbbās read: ”واذَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ“; and ”اَلْأمَهُ“ is forgetfulness. One says: ”أمِهَ، يَأْمَهُ، أمَهًا“ — this is correct, with fatḥa of the mīm. Some narrated from Abū ʿUbayda: ”أمْهٌ“ with sukūn of the mīm, but that is not soundly [transmitted] from him, because the maṣdar is ”يَأْمَهُ، أمَهًا“ and nothing else.
[Translator's note: The source says Ibn ʿAbbās read «واذَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ» and then explains «اَلْأمَهُ» (forgetfulness); the reading attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās is generally reported as «بَعْدَ أمَهٍ». Translated as written.]
Al-Ḥasan read: ”أنا آتِيكم بِتَأْوِيلِهِ“, and I dislike it for its contradiction of the muṣḥaf. ”اِدَّكَرَ“ is in origin ”واِذْتَكَرَ“, but the tāʾ was replaced by dāl, and the dhāl was assimilated into the dāl. ”واذَّكَرَ“ with dhāl is permissible, but the dāl is better.

zajjaj:46-46.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يُوسُفُ أيُّها الصِّدِّيقُ﴾: he meant "O Yūsuf". In the vocative (nidāʾ) of a definite noun, eliding ”يا“ is permissible, so you say: "O Zayd, come forward" and "Zayd, come forward". The poet said:
؎مُحَمَّدُ تَفْدِ نَفْسَكَ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ إذا ما خِفْتَ مِن أمْرٍ تَبالا
(Muḥammad, may every soul ransom your soul, whenever you fear ruin from some affair.)
He meant "O Muḥammad". ”اَلصِّدِّيقُ“ is the one who is extreme in truthfulness and in affirming the truth.
His saying: ﴿لَعَلِّي أرْجِعُ إلى النّاسِ لَعَلَّهم يَعْلَمُونَ﴾, that is: perhaps they will know the interpretation of the king's dream; and it may be: perhaps they will know your standing, and that will be the cause of your release from prison.

zajjaj:47-47.t:
﴿قالَ تَزْرَعُونَ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ دَأبًا﴾, that is: you will persist diligently (tadʾabūna daʾaban); ”تَزْرَعُونَ“ points to ”تَدْأبُونَ“. ”اَلدَّأبُ“ is constant adherence to something, and habit.
His saying: ﴿وَفِيهِ يَعْصِرُونَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 49]; it has also been read: ”وَفِيهِ يُعْصَرُونَ“. Whoever says ”وَفِيهِ يَعْصِرُونَ“ with yāʾ [means]: "after fourteen years the year will come in which people will be given rain, and in it they will press oil and grapes". Whoever reads ”يُعْصَرُونَ“ means "they will be rained upon", from His saying: ﴿وَأنْـزَلْنا مِنَ المُعْصِراتِ ماءً ثَجّاجًا﴾ [al-Nabaʾ: 14]. Whoever reads ”وَفِيهِ تَعْصِرُونَ“: if he wishes, it is on the interpretation of ”يَعْصِرُونَ“, and if he wishes, it is on the interpretation of: "and in it you will be saved from affliction and take refuge in plenty". ʿAdī ibn Zayd said:
؎لَوْ بِغَيْرِ الماءِ حَلْقِي شَرِقٌ كُنْتُ كالغِصّانِ بِالماءِ اعْتِصارِي
(Were my throat choking on something other than water, [water would be my refuge] — but I am like one choking on water: [where then is] my refuge?)
One says: "so-and-so is in a ʿaṣar" and "in a ʿuṣra" when he is in a fortress that cannot be overcome.

zajjaj:50-50.t:
His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿وَقالَ المَلِكُ ائْتُونِي بِهِ﴾: when he was informed of his standing in knowledge of interpretation, he sought him. ﴿قالَ ارْجِعْ إلى رَبِّكَ فاسْألْهُ﴾, that is: to your master; ”رَبُّ الشَّيْءِ“ (the rabb of a thing) is its owner.
﴿فاسْألْهُ ما بالُ النِّسْوَةِ اللاتِي قَطَّعْنَ أيْدِيَهُنَّ﴾; ”اَللّائِي قَطَّعْنَ“ is also permissible. That is: "ask him to yastaʿmil the soundness of my innocence of what I was accused of".
[Translator's note: «أنْ يَسْتَعْمِلَ» literally means "to make use of"; the context suggests "to ascertain" (perhaps «يَسْتَعْلِمَ»). Translated as written.]
It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: «"Had I been in Yūsuf's place and then the messenger had come to me, I would have hastened to him"». He ﷺ admired Yūsuf's resolve and patience when the king summoned him: he did not hasten to him until he knew that the soundness of his innocence had been established with the king.

zajjaj:51-51.t:
﴿قالَ ما خَطْبُكُنَّ إذْ راوَدْتُنَّ يُوسُفَ﴾: Yūsuf, upon him be peace, did not single out the wife of al-ʿAzīz by name, out of good companionship and courtesy on his part, so he included her among the women.
[Translator's note: The Quranic words here are spoken by the king; the source's remark refers to Yūsuf's earlier request (verse 50) mentioning only «النِّسْوَةِ». Translated as written.]
His saying: ﴿قُلْنَ حاشَ لِلَّهِ ما عَلِمْنا عَلَيْهِ مِن سُوءٍ﴾: it has been read ”حاشَ لِلَّهِ“ and ”حاشا لِلَّهِ“, and al-Ḥasan read ”حاشْ لِلَّهِ“ with sukūn of the shīn. There is no disagreement among the grammarians that the quiescence is not permissible, because combining two quiescent letters is not permissible, nor is it of the speech of the Arabs. ﴿ما عَلِمْنا عَلَيْهِ مِن سُوءٍ﴾: so the women informed the king of Yūsuf's innocence. ﴿قالَتِ امْرَأتُ العَزِيزِ الآنَ حَصْحَصَ الحَقُّ﴾, that is: it has emerged and become clear. Its derivation in the language is from ”اَلْحِصَّةُ“ (share, portion), that is: the share of the truth and its side have become distinct from the side of falsehood.

zajjaj:52-52.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أنِّي لَمْ أخُنْهُ بِالغَيْبِ﴾: this is the saying of Yūsuf, upon him be peace. The meaning is: "I wanted to make clear to the king the matter of his wife and the women, so that he would know that I did not betray him in secret". ”ذَلِكَ“ is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or, if you wish, as the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ, as if he said: "my affair is that". It is narrated that Jibrīl, upon him be peace, said to him: "Not even when you undid the waistband?" — and it has been said: "Not even when you inclined?" — so he said: ﴿وَما أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِي إنَّ النَّفْسَ لأمّارَةٌ بِالسُّوءِ إلا ما رَحِمَ رَبِّي﴾ [Yūsuf: 53]. The position of ”ما“ is accusative as an exception (istithnāʾ).

zajjaj:54-54.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أسْتَخْلِصْهُ لِنَفْسِي﴾ is jussive (majzūm), as the answer to the command (jawāb al-amr). The meaning of ”أسْتَخْلِصْهُ“ is: I will make him exclusively mine, no one sharing him with me. ﴿فَلَمّا كَلَّمَهُ قالَ إنَّكَ اليَوْمَ لَدَيْنا مَكِينٌ أمِينٌ﴾, that is: we have come to know your trustworthiness and your innocence of what you were accused of.

zajjaj:55-55.t: ﴿قالَ اجْعَلْنِي عَلى خَزائِنِ الأرْضِ﴾, that is: over its wealth. ﴿إنِّي حَفِيظٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾, that is: I will guard it and I know the ways of its disposal. He only asked him to put him over the storehouses of the land because the prophets were sent to establish truth and justice and to put things in their proper places; and Yūsuf, upon him be peace, knew that there was no one more upright in that than he, nor better at putting it in its proper places, so he asked for that out of a desire for the common good.

zajjaj:59-59.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلَمّا جَهَّزَهم بِجَهازِهِمْ قالَ ائْتُونِي بِأخٍ لَكم مِن أبِيكُمْ﴾: this — and Allah knows best — was preceded by talk that led to what necessitated asking them for their brother, because he would not say "Bring me a brother of yours from your father" without something having occurred that necessitated this saying. So it is as if — and Allah knows best — he asked them about their news, their affairs and their number, and so he ventured to make this request.
﴿ألا تَرَوْنَ أنِّي أُوفِي الكَيْلَ وأنا خَيْرُ المُنْـزِلِينَ﴾: because when he lodged them, he hosted them well.

zajjaj:60-60.t: His saying: ﴿فَإنْ لَمْ تَأْتُونِي بِهِ فَلا كَيْلَ لَكم عِنْدِي ولا تَقْرَبُونِ﴾: the reading is with kasra of the nūn, and fatḥa — with fatḥa of the nūn — is permissible, because it is the nūn of the plural, as He said: ﴿فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 54] with fatḥa of the nūn. Then ”وَلا تَقْرَبُونَ“ has the wording of a statement and the meaning of a command.

zajjaj:61-61.t: ﴿قالُوا سَنُراوِدُ عَنْهُ أباهُ وإنّا لَفاعِلُونَ﴾: ”وَإنّا لَفاعِلُونَ“ is emphasis (tawkīd).

zajjaj:62-62.t: ﴿وَقالَ لِفِتْيانِهِ﴾ and ”لِفِتْيَتِهِ“ — both have been read. ”اَلْفِتْيانُ“ and ”اَلْفِتْيَةُ“ are the slaves in this place. ﴿اجْعَلُوا بِضاعَتَهم في رِحالِهِمْ لَعَلَّهم يَعْرِفُونَها إذا انْقَلَبُوا إلى أهْلِهِمْ لَعَلَّهم يَرْجِعُونَ﴾: there are two ways in this. That is: when they see their merchandise returned to them, they will know that the price of the food measured out for them was not taken from them, and that placing the merchandise in the saddlebags was only by Yūsuf's order. And it may be that ”لَعَلَّهم يَرْجِعُونَ“ means: they will return the merchandise, because it is the price of what they had measured out, and because they do not take anything except for its price.

zajjaj:63-63.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَأرْسِلْ مَعَنا أخانا نَكْتَلْ وإنّا لَهُ لَحافِظُونَ﴾, that is: if you send him with us, we will obtain measure; otherwise we have been denied the measure.

zajjaj:64-64.t: ﴿قالَ هَلْ آمَنُكم عَلَيْهِ إلا كَما أمِنتُكم عَلى أخِيهِ مِن قَبْلُ﴾, that is: you said the same to me about Yūsuf: "Send him with us tomorrow, he will enjoy himself and play, and we will surely guard him"; you guaranteed me Yūsuf's safekeeping, and such is this guarantee of yours in my eyes. ”فاللَّهُ خَيْرٌ حِفْظًا“ — it is also read ﴿حافِظًا﴾. ”حِفْظًا“ is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), and ”حافِظًا“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); ”حافِظًا“ may also be a tamyīz.

zajjaj:65-65.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَجَدُوا بِضاعَتَهم رُدَّتْ إلَيْهِمْ﴾; it is also read ”رِدَّتْ“ with kasra of the rāʾ. The origin is ”رُدِدَتْ“; the first dāl was assimilated into the second, and the rāʾ remained with ḍamma. Whoever gives the rāʾ kasra makes its kasra transferred from the dāl, as was done in ”قِيلَ“ and ”بِيعَ“, to indicate that the original vowel of the dāl is kasra. Quṭrub related that in ”ضُرِبَ زَيْدٌ“ (Zayd was struck) one says ”ضُرْبَ زَيْدٌ“ and ”ضِرْبَ زَيْدٌ“ with kasra of the ḍād: he made the rāʾ quiescent and transferred its kasra to the ḍād.
According to this dialect, ”كِبْدٌ“ is permissible for ”كَبِدٌ“.
﴿قالُوا يا أبانا ما نَبْغِي﴾, that is: what do we want? ”ما“ is in the position of the accusative; the meaning is: what [more] would we want, when our merchandise has been returned to us? It may also be that ”ما“ is negation, as if they said: "we do not want anything". ﴿هَذِهِ بِضاعَتُنا رُدَّتْ إلَيْنا ونَمِيرُ أهْلَنا﴾: one says ”مِرْتُهُمْ، أمِيرُهُمْ، مَيْرًا“ when you bring them provisions (mīra). ﴿وَنَـزْدادُ كَيْلَ بَعِيرٍ﴾: because each man used to be measured a camel-load. ﴿ذَلِكَ كَيْلٌ يَسِيرٌ﴾, that is: "that is an easy measure", that is: easy for the one to whom he goes.

zajjaj:66-66.t: ﴿إلا أنْ يُحاطَ بِكُمْ﴾: the position of ”أنْ“ is accusative, and the meaning is: you will surely bring him to me, except on account of being surrounded, that is: you shall not refrain from bringing him except for this. This is called a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). ”إلّا“ here comes in the sense of realising the recompense; you say: "you come only to take the dirhams" and "only that you take the dirhams". The meaning of their being surrounded is that they are prevented from [reaching] him, so they are unable to bring him.

zajjaj:67-67.t: ﴿وَقالَ يا بَنِيَّ لا تَدْخُلُوا مِن بابٍ واحِدٍ وادْخُلُوا مِن أبْوابٍ مُتَفَرِّقَةٍ﴾: he feared the evil eye for them, and the matter of the evil eye is true — and Allah knows best. It has been narrated «from the Prophet ﷺ that he sought protection for al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, saying in his supplication: "I seek protection for you both from every harmful eye"».

zajjaj:68-68.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَمّا دَخَلُوا مِن حَيْثُ أمَرَهم أبُوهم ما كانَ يُغْنِي عَنْهم مِنَ اللَّهِ مِن شَيْءٍ إلا حاجَةً في نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ قَضاها﴾, that is: except the fear of the evil eye. The interpretation of ”ما كانَ يُغْنِي عَنْهم مِنَ اللَّهِ مِن شَيْءٍ“ is: had it been decreed that it strike them, it would have struck them while separated just as it would strike them together. And it may be: nothing avails against the decree of Allah. ﴿وَإنَّهُ لَذُو عِلْمٍ لِما عَلَّمْناهُ﴾, that is: possessed of knowledge because of Our teaching him. ”حاجَةً“ is accusative as an exception not of the same kind as the first [i.e. a disjoined exception], the meaning being: "but a need in Yaʿqūb's soul which he fulfilled".

zajjaj:69-69.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿آوى إلَيْهِ أخاهُ﴾, that is: he drew his brother close to himself. ﴿فَلا تَبْتَئِسْ﴾, that is: do not grieve and do not be downcast.

zajjaj:70-70.t:
﴿فَلَمّا جَهَّزَهم بِجَهازِهِمْ جَعَلَ السِّقايَةَ في رَحْلِ أخِيهِ ثُمَّ أذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ﴾, that is: an announcer announced. One says: ”آذَنْتُهُ بِالشَّيْءِ، فَهو مُؤْذَنٌ بِهِ“, that is: I informed him; and ”أذَنْتُ“: I announced the thing repeatedly. ﴿أيَّتُها العِيرُ إنَّكم لَسارِقُونَ﴾: the meaning is: "O you, companions of the caravan"; but he said ”أيَّتُها العِيرُ“ meaning "the people of the caravan", as He said: ﴿واسْألِ القَرْيَةَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 82], meaning the people of the town. And he made ”أيُّ“ feminine because he assigned it to "the caravan" (al-ʿīr).
[Translator's note: «أذَنْتُ» is as written; the intensive form is usually «أذَّنْتُ».]

zajjaj:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿قالُوا نَفْقِدُ صُواعَ المَلِكِ﴾; it has been read ”صَواعَ المَلِكِ“ and ”صاعَ المَلِكِ“; Abū Hurayra read ”صاغَ المَلِكِ“; and it has been read ”صَوْغَ المَلِكِ“, with dotted ghayn. ﴿وَلِمَن جاءَ بِهِ حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ﴾, that is: a camel-load of food. ﴿وَأنا بِهِ زَعِيمٌ﴾, that is: guarantor. ”اَلصُّواعُ“ is the ṣāʿ itself, and it is treated as masculine and feminine; likewise ”اَلصّاعُ“ is treated as masculine and feminine. It has come in the exegesis that it was an elongated vessel resembling the makkūk [a measuring vessel], from which the king used to drink, and it is the drinking-cup (al-siqāya). It has been said that it was made of silver plated with gold; it has been said that it was of mis (copper); and it has been said that it resembled a bowl (ṭās).
[Translator's note: The source has «مِن مَسٍّ»; read here as «مِسّ» (copper).]

zajjaj:73-73.t: ﴿قالُوا تاللَّهِ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمْ ما جِئْنا لِنُفْسِدَ في الأرْضِ﴾: the meaning of ”تاللَّهِ“ is ”واللَّهِ“ (by Allah), except that the oath is not sworn with the tāʾ except with "Allah"; ”تالرَّحْمَنِ“ is not permissible, nor ”تَرَبِّي لَأفْعَلَنَّ“. The tāʾ is a substitute for the wāw, as they said ”تُراثٌ“ for ”وُراثٍ“, and as they said ”يَتَّزِنُ“, whose origin is ”يَوْتَزِنُ“, from ”اَلْوَزْنُ“. They only said ”لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمْ ما جِئْنا لِنُفْسِدَ في الأرْضِ“ because they would not alight upon a people unjustly, nor graze anyone's crops, and they put muzzles on the mouths of their camels so that they would not meddle with crops. And they said: ﴿وَما كُنّا سارِقِينَ﴾ because, according to what has been narrated, they had returned the merchandise they found in their saddlebags; that is: how can one who returns what he found be a thief?

zajjaj:74-74.t:
﴿قالُوا فَما جَزاؤُهُ إنْ كُنْتُمْ كاذِبِينَ﴾ ﴿قالُوا جَزاؤُهُ مَن وُجِدَ في رَحْلِهِ فَهو جَزاؤُهُ كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي الظّالِمِينَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 75], that is: with the like of this recompense We recompense the wrongdoers. The recompense of the thief among them was that he be enslaved for his theft — he becomes a slave because he stole.
As for the nominative of ”قالُوا جَزاؤُهُ مَن وُجِدَ في رَحْلِهِ“, it is from two angles. One of them is that ”هُوَ جَزاؤُهُ“ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ”مَن وُجِدَ في رَحْلِهِ“ is the khabar (predicate), the meaning being: "the recompense for the theft is the person in whose saddlebag the stolen thing is found"; and His saying ”فَهُوَ جَزاؤُهُ“ is an addition for clarity, as you say: "The recompense of the thief is the cutting [of the hand]; that is his recompense; this is his recompense" — as an addition for clarity.
[Translator's note: The source writes «أنَّ "هُوَ جَزاؤُهُ"، اِبْتِداءٌ»; from the analysis that follows, the mubtadaʾ meant is evidently the first «جَزاؤُهُ». Translated as written.]
And it may be that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with ”مَن وُجِدَ في رَحْلِهِ فَهو جَزاؤُهُ“ — this clause — being the khabar of "the recompense", the pronoun-link (ʿāʾid) to it from the clause being ”جَزاؤُهُ“ that comes after His saying ”فَهُوَ“; as if it were said: "They said: its recompense — the one in whose saddlebag it is found, he is it", that is: "he is the recompense". But the overt [noun] was better here, so that no ambiguity would occur in the speech, and so that it would not be imagined that ”هُوَ“, if it recurred a second time, did not refer back to "the recompense". When the Arabs give emphatic prominence to the matter of a thing, they make the link to it a repetition of its very wording. All the grammarians recited:
؎لا أرى المَوْتَ يَسْبِقُ المَوْتَ شَيْءٌ نَغَّصَ المَوْتُ ذا الغِنى والفَقِيرا
(I see that nothing outstrips death; death has troubled both the rich and the poor.)
and he did not say: "I see that nothing outstrips it".

zajjaj:76-76.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَخْرَجَها مِن وِعاءِ أخِيهِ﴾: the feminine refers back to the drinking-cup (al-siqāya); and it may be that he treated al-ṣuwāʿ as feminine. ﴿كَذَلِكَ كِدْنا لِيُوسُفَ ما كانَ لِيَأْخُذَ أخاهُ في دِينِ المَلِكِ﴾, that is: in the custom of the king and what the king follows as law, because in the king's law the thief was fined twice what he stole.
Among the family of Yaʿqūb, and in their way, the thief became a slave, enslaved by the owner of the stolen thing. ﴿إلا أنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ﴾: the position of ”أنْ“ is accusative; when the bāʾ dropped out, the verb reached it directly and put it in the accusative. The meaning is: "he could not take his brother under the king's law except by the will of Allah". ”نَرْفَعُ دَرَجاتِ مَن نَشاءُ“ is by annexing "degrees" to ”مَن“; ”دَرَجاتٍ“ with tanwīn is also permissible, with ”مَن“ in the position of the accusative, the meaning being: "We raise whom We will by degrees".
The nominative ”دَرَجاتٌ مَن نَشاءُ“ is also permissible and is good, but I do not know that it has been narrated, so do not ever read it unless a sound narration of it is established. ﴿وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾: it was said in the exegesis: "above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing", until knowledge ends with Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

zajjaj:77-77.t:
﴿قالُوا إنْ يَسْرِقْ فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أخٌ لَهُ مِن قَبْلُ﴾: they mean Yūsuf. It is narrated that in his childhood he took an image made of gold, of the things with which some of those opposed to the people of the religion of Islam used to worship; and his taking it was by way of disapproval, so that such a thing would not be venerated. ﴿فَأسَرَّها يُوسُفُ في نَفْسِهِ ولَمْ يُبْدِها لَهُمْ﴾, that is: he did not show it to them. ﴿قالَ أنْتُمْ شَرٌّ مَكانًا﴾
This is a pronoun used on condition of later explanation (iḍmār ʿalā sharīṭat al-tafsīr), because His saying ”قالَ أنْتُمْ شَرٌّ مَكانًا“ is a badal (substitute) for the ”ها“ in His saying ﴿فَأسَرَّها﴾. The meaning is: "So Yūsuf kept secret within himself his saying: ﴿أنْتُمْ شَرٌّ مَكانًا﴾". The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: you are in a worse position in theft, in truth, because you stole your brother from your father. ﴿واللَّهُ أعْلَمُ بِما تَصِفُونَ﴾, that is: "Allah knows best whether a brother of his stole or not".

zajjaj:78-78.t: ﴿قالُوا يا أيُّها العَزِيزُ﴾: ”اَلْعَزِيزُ“ is the king. ﴿إنَّ لَهُ أبًا شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا﴾: ”شَيْخًا“ is a naʿt (adjective) of ”أبًا“; ”أبًا“ is accusative by ”إنَّ“; and ”كَبِيرًا“ is a naʿt of ”شَيْخًا“. ﴿فَخُذْ أحَدَنا مَكانَهُ إنّا نَراكَ مِنَ المُحْسِنِينَ﴾, that is: of those who act generously and do not deal strictly by the letter in what is due, because he had given them the food and given them its price by returning the merchandise to them; so they asked him to act generously.

zajjaj:79-79.t: ﴿قالَ مَعاذَ اللَّهِ أنْ نَأْخُذَ إلا مَن وجَدْنا مَتاعَنا عِنْدَهُ﴾: ”مَعاذَ اللَّهِ“ is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. mafʿūl muṭlaq], the meaning being: "I seek refuge in Allah with a seeking of refuge". The position of ”أنْ“ is accusative; the meaning is: I seek refuge in Allah from taking anyone except the one with whom we found our property; when ”مِن“ dropped out, the verb reached it directly and put it in the accusative. ﴿إنّا إذًا لَظالِمُونَ﴾, that is: if we took someone else, we would be wrongdoers.

zajjaj:80-80.t:
﴿فَلَمّا اسْتَيْأسُوا مِنهُ خَلَصُوا نَجِيًّا﴾: the meaning is: they withdrew conferring privately, that is: they withdrew as people conferring privately about what they would do in going to their father without their brother with them. ”نَجِيٌّ“ is a singular word with a plural meaning; likewise ﴿وَإذْ هم نَجْوى﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 47]. One may say ”قَوْمٌ نَجِيٌّ“, ”قَوْمٌ نَجْوى“ and ”قَوْمٌ أنْجِيَةٌ“. The poet said:
؎إنِّي إذا ما القَوْمُ صارُوا أنْجِيَةْ
؎واخْتَلَفَ القَوْلُ اخْتِلافَ الأرْشِيَةْ
؎هُناكَ أوْصِينِي ولا تُوصِي بِيَهْ
(When the people become groups conferring in secret, and talk goes back and forth like well-ropes, then entrust [matters] to me, and do not entrust me [to others].)
The meaning of ”خَلَصُوا“ is: they went apart, their brother not being with them.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَمِن قَبْلُ ما فَرَّطْتُمْ في يُوسُفَ﴾: the best of the ways is that ”ما“ is redundant (laghw), so the meaning is: "and before, you failed in your duty concerning Yūsuf". It may be that ”ما“ is in the position of the nominative, so the meaning is: "and before [was] your failure concerning Yūsuf", that is: "your failure concerning Yūsuf occurred". And it may be that ”ما“ is in the position of the accusative, conjoined (nasaq) to ”أنَّ“, the meaning being: "Do you not know that your father … and know your failure concerning Yūsuf?" ﴿فَلَنْ أبْرَحَ الأرْضَ حَتّى يَأْذَنَ لِي أبِي﴾, that is: I will not leave the land of Egypt — otherwise all people are on the earth. ﴿أوْ يَحْكُمَ اللَّهُ لِي﴾ is conjoined to ”حَتّى يَأْذَنَ“; and it may be that ”أوْ“ is as the answer to ”لَنْ“, the meaning being: "I will not leave the land until Allah judges for me".

zajjaj:81-81.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ ابْنَكَ سَرَقَ﴾; ”سُرِّقَ“ is also permissible, though ”سَرَقَ“ is firmer in the reading. ”سُرِّقَ“ may be of two kinds: ”سُرِّقَ“: it became known that he stole; and ”سُرِّقَ“: he was accused of theft.

zajjaj:83-83.t: ﴿قالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكم أنْفُسُكُمْ﴾, that is: your souls have made [it] seem fair to you, and your souls have endeared [it] to you. ﴿فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ﴾: the meaning is "my affair is beautiful patience", or "my patience is beautiful patience". We have explained this earlier in the sūra.

zajjaj:84-84.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يا أسَفى عَلى يُوسُفَ﴾: its meaning is "O my grief!". The origin is ”يا أسَفِي“, except that the yāʾ of annexation may be replaced by alif because of the lightness of the alif and the fatḥa. ﴿فَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ﴾, that is: grief-stricken.

zajjaj:85-85.t:
﴿قالُوا تاللَّهِ تَفْتَأُ تَذْكُرُ يُوسُفَ﴾: the meaning of ”تاللَّهِ“ is ”واللَّهِ“ (by Allah), and ”لا“ is implied (muḍmara); the meaning is: "By Allah, you will not cease remembering Yūsuf", that is: "you will continue remembering Yūsuf". ﴿حَتّى تَكُونَ حَرَضًا﴾: ”اَلْحَرَضُ“ is one corrupted in his body, that is: "until you are wasting and sick"; and ”اَلْحَرَضُ“ is one corrupted in his character. Their saying "I incited (ḥarraḍtu) so-and-so against so-and-so" is to be interpreted as: I corrupted him against him.
The implying of ”لا“ in His saying ”تاللَّهِ تَفْتَأُ تَذْكُرُ يُوسُفَ“ is permissible only because in the oath ”تاللَّهِ تَفْعَلُ“ is not permissible unless you say ”لَتَفْعَلَنَّ“ or ”لا تَفْعَلْ“.
[Translator's note: «لا تَفْعَلْ» is as written (with jussive sukūn); in an oath the negated form is normally «لا تَفْعَلُ».]
Swearing oaths is not permissible for people except by Allah, Mighty and Majestic. A man may not swear by his father, nor ought he to swear by the prophets; he should swear only by Allah. It is narrated «from the Prophet, upon him be peace, that he said to ʿUmar: "Do not swear by your fathers; whoever swears, let him swear by Allah"».
If someone says: What then is the sense of the oath in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His saying: ﴿واللَّيْلِ إذا يَغْشى﴾ [al-Layl: 1], ﴿والسَّماءِ ذاتِ البُرُوجِ﴾ [al-Burūj: 1], ﴿والتِّينِ والزَّيْتُونِ﴾ [al-Tīn: 1], and the like of these things which Allah, Majestic is His majesty, mentioned in His Book? There are several ways concerning them, all of which the Basrans mentioned. They said: it may be that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, swore by them because in all of them there is evidence pointing to Him and clear signs. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إنَّ في خَلْقِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ واخْتِلافِ اللَّيْلِ والنَّهارِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 164] — to the end of the verse.
And He said: ﴿وَفِي خَلْقِكم وما يَبُثُّ مِن دابَّةٍ آياتٌ﴾ [al-Jāthiya: 4]. So the oath by these indicates the greatness of Allah. Quṭrub said: it may be that its meaning is "by the Lord of the sun and its morning brightness", "by the Lord of the fig and the olive", as He said: ﴿والسَّماءِ ذاتِ البُرُوجِ﴾ [al-Burūj: 1], and He said: ﴿والأرْضِ وما طَحاها﴾ [al-Shams: 6],
and He said: ﴿فَوَرَبِّ السَّماءِ والأرْضِ إنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 23]. They also said: it may be "by the creation of the heavens and the earth", "by the creation of the fig and the olive". And they said: it may be that, since the meaning of an oath is the meaning of affirmation, and these things by which Allah swore are all real, likewise what He swore about is real; so the meaning is: "Just as the fig and the olive are real, We have certainly created man in the best stature". The best of these views is the one we began with first.

zajjaj:88-88.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَجِئْنا بِبِضاعَةٍ مُزْجاةٍ﴾: they said ”مُزْجاةٍ“ means scanty. They said: they had brought Bedouin goods such as wool, clarified butter and the like, of what Bedouins sell. It has been said that the merchandise was of a kind whose like does not sell for food, because Bedouin goods were like that — low-grade wealth lay beneath them. Its interpretation in the language is that ”اَلتَّزْجِيَةُ“ is the small thing with which one gets by. You say: "so-and-so yuzajjī his living", that is: he gets by with little and makes do with it. So the meaning on this view is: "We have brought merchandise with which one can only get by", that is: "subsist", "not of that with which one lives in ease". The poet said:
؎اَلْواهِبُ المِائَةَ الهِجانَ وعَبْدَها عُوذُوا تُزَجِّي خَلْفَها أطْفالَها
(The giver of a hundred pure-white camels with their herdsman, recently foaled, driving their young along behind them.)
that is: driving their young along.

zajjaj:90-90.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قالُوا أإنَّكَ لأنْتَ يُوسُفُ﴾: there are four ways in it: combining the two hamzas, ”قالُوا أئِنَّكَ“, pronouncing both fully; ”أيِنَّكَ“ is permissible, making the second between yāʾ and hamza; it has been read ”آئِنَّكَ“ [i.e. the question hamza] onto ”إنَّكَ“, separating the two hamzas with an alif because of the meeting of the two hamzas. The poet said:
؎أيا ظَبْيَةَ الوَعْساءِ بَيْنَ جَلاجِلٍ وبَيْنَ النَّقا آأنْتِ أمْ أُمُّ سالِمِ
(O gazelle of the sandy ground between Jalājil and the dune — is it you, or Umm Sālim?)
And ”قالُوا إنَّكَ لَأنْتَ“ in the form of a statement is permissible.

zajjaj:92-92.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لا تَثْرِيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ اليَوْمَ﴾, that is: no spoiling [of you] is upon you.

zajjaj:94-94.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لَوْلا أنْ تُفَنِّدُونِ﴾: its meaning is: were it not that you would call me ignorant; and ”تُسَفِّهُونِ“ (call me foolish) is also narrated.

zajjaj:97-97.t:
His saying: ﴿إنّا كُنّا خاطِئِينَ﴾: one says ”قَدْ خَطِئَ، يَخْطَأُ، خَطَأً، وخَطْأً“ (he sinned / erred intentionally) and ”أخْطَأ، يُخْطِئُ، إخْطاءً“ (he erred). Imruʾ al-Qays said:
؎يا لَهْفَ هِنْدٍ إذْ خَطِئْنَ كاهِلًا اَلْقاتِلِينَ المَلِكَ الحُلاحِلا
(Alas for Hind, when they [the horses] missed Kāhil, the slayers of the noble, lordly king!)

zajjaj:98-98.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿سَوْفَ أسْتَغْفِرُ لَكم رَبِّي﴾: Yaʿqūb said that intending to seek forgiveness for them at the time of the onset of the pre-dawn (saḥar), the time that is for the answering of supplication — not that he was stingy with seeking forgiveness. That is more in keeping with the character of the prophets, I mean exerting oneself in seeking forgiveness and deliberately choosing the time of answering.

zajjaj:99-99.t: ﴿آوى إلَيْهِ أبَوَيْهِ﴾, that is: he drew his parents close to himself.

zajjaj:100-100.t: ﴿وَرَفَعَ أبَوَيْهِ عَلى العَرْشِ﴾: ”اَلْعَرْشُ“ is the throne-couch (al-sarīr). ﴿وَخَرُّوا لَهُ سُجَّدًا﴾: it was part of the custom of honouring at that time to prostrate to the one honoured. And it has been said: ”وَخَرُّوا لَهُ سُجَّدًا“ means "and they fell down [prostrating] to Allah".

zajjaj:101-101.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿رَبِّ قَدْ آتَيْتَنِي مِنَ المُلْكِ وعَلَّمْتَنِي مِن تَأْوِيلِ الأحادِيثِ﴾: there are two views on it — I mean on the entry of ”مِن“. It may be that he meant: You have taught me some of the interpretation and given me some of the kingship; and it may be that ”مِن“ enters to distinguish this genus from all other genera, so the meaning is: "My Lord, You have given me kingship and taught me the interpretation of accounts", like His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿تُؤْتِي المُلْكَ مَن تَشاءُ وتَنْـزِعُ المُلْكَ مِمَّنْ تَشاءُ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 26]. [This] indicates that ”مِن“ here is only for specifying the genus (tabyīn al-jins). Like it is His saying: ﴿فاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الأوْثانِ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 30]: they were not commanded to avoid some of the idols; rather the meaning is: "avoid the filth which is the idols".
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فاطِرَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾ is accusative in two ways. One of them is as an attribute, by His saying ”رَبِّ قَدْ آتَيْتَنِي مِنَ المُلْكِ“, the meaning being "O my Lord, You have given me": this is an annexed vocative in the position of the accusative, and ”فاطِرَ السَّمَواتِ والأرْضِ“ is an attribute of the first. And it may be accusative as a second vocative, so the meaning is: "O Originator of the heavens and the earth". ﴿أنْتَ ولِيِّي﴾
﴿وَألْحِقْنِي بِالصّالِحِينَ﴾, that is: join me to their ranks of Your mercy and Your forgiveness.

zajjaj:102-102.t:
﴿ذَلِكَ مِن أنْباءِ الغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إلَيْكَ﴾: this is an address to the Prophet, upon him be peace. The meaning is: "What We have related to you of the matter of Yūsuf and his brothers is of the reports that were hidden from you". So it was sent down upon him as a proof establishing his prophethood, as a warning, and as an easing by detailing the stories of past nations. The position of ”ذَلِكَ“ is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being ”مِن أنْباءِ الغَيْبِ“, and ”نُوحِيهِ إلَيْكَ“ a second khabar. If you wish, you may make ”نُوحِيهِ“ the khabar and put ”ذَلِكَ“ in the place of ”اَلَّذِي“ (which), the meaning being: "That which is of the reports of the unseen, We reveal it to you".
[Translator's note: The source's final paraphrase reads «اَلَّذِي مِن أنْباءِ الغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إلَيْكَ ذَلِكَ», with «ذَلِكَ» placed at the end; rendered by sense.]

zajjaj:103-103.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَما أكْثَرُ النّاسِ ولَوْ حَرَصْتَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: its meaning is: "Most people are not believers, even if you were eager to guide them, because you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills".

zajjaj:104-104.t: ﴿وَما تَسْألُهم عَلَيْهِ مِن أجْرٍ﴾, that is: "You do not ask them any wage for the Qur'an, its recitation and your guiding them". ﴿إنْ هو إلا ذِكْرٌ لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾, that is: "It is only a reminder to them of what is their well-being, their deliverance from the Fire, their entering Paradise, their being warned and given good tidings; all well-being is in it".

zajjaj:105-105.t:
﴿وَكَأيِّنْ مِن آيَةٍ في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾, that is: of a sign and an indication that points them to the oneness of Allah: of the matter of the sky — that it is without pillars and does not fall upon the earth, and that it contains the courses of the sun and the moon that it contains; in it is the greatest proof and evidence that the One who created it is one, and that it has a Creator — and likewise in what is witnessed on the earth, of its plants, its seas and its mountains. ﴿وَهم عَنْها مُعْرِضُونَ﴾, that is: they do not reflect on what points them to the oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and the proof that they do not reflect on that by which they would infer
[Translator's note: The source text breaks off here mid-sentence.]

zajjaj:106-106.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَما يُؤْمِنُ أكْثَرُهم بِاللَّهِ إلا وهم مُشْرِكُونَ﴾, that is: if they acknowledged that Allah is their Creator and the Creator of the heavens and the earth, they associated idols in His worship, and they associated [things] other than idols.

zajjaj:107-107.t: ﴿أفَأمِنُوا أنْ تَأْتِيَهم غاشِيَةٌ مِن عَذابِ اللَّهِ﴾, that is: that there come to them punishment that overpowers them. ﴿أوْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ السّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً﴾, that is: suddenly. ”بَغْتَةً“ is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). You say: "I met him baghtatan and fajʾatan", and its meaning is: from where I did not expect to meet him.

zajjaj:109-109.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلَدارُ الآخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا﴾, and in more than one place: ﴿وَلَلدّارُ الآخِرَةُ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 32]. Whoever says ”اَلدّارُ الآخِرَةُ“, then ”اَلْآخِرَةُ“ is a naʿt (adjective) of "the abode", because all creatures have two abodes: the abode in which they were created, which is this world, and the last abode, in which they are brought back as a new creation. Whoever says ”دارُ الآخِرَةِ“, it is as if he said "the abode of the last life", because people have two lives: the life of this world and the life of the Hereafter. The like of this in speech is ”اَلصَّلاةُ الأُولى“ and ”صَلاةُ الأُولى“: whoever says ”اَلصَّلاةُ الأُولى“ makes ”اَلْأُولى“ a naʿt of the prayer, and whoever says ”صَلاةُ الأُولى“ means "the prayer of the first obligatory [prayer]" and "the first hour".

zajjaj:110-110.t:
﴿حَتّى إذا اسْتَيْئَسَ الرُّسُلُ وظَنُّوا أنَّهم قَدْ كُذِبُوا﴾: it has been read ”كُذِبُوا“ and ”كُذِّبُوا“, with the light and the doubled [dhāl], and it has been read ”وَكَذَبُوا“. As for whoever reads ”وَظَنُّوا أنَّهم قَدْ كُذِّبُوا“ with the doubling, the meaning is: "until, when the messengers despaired of their people believing them, Our help came to them". And whoever reads ”قَدْ كُذِبُوا“ with the light [dhāl], the meaning is: "and their people thought that they [the messengers] had been told a lie in what they were promised", because the messengers would not think that.
Some said: "and they thought that they had been failed (ukhlifū)", that is, the messengers thought so; that is far-fetched as a description of the messengers. It is narrated from ʿĀʾisha that the Prophet ﷺ was never promised anything in which he was failed, and in the report: "Allah forbid that the messengers should think this of their Lord". And the meaning of ”وَظَنُّوا أنَّهم قَدْ [كَذَبُوا]“ is: "their people also thought that they [the messengers] had lied".
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَنُجِّيَ مَن نَشاءُ﴾: it has been read ”فَنُنَجِّي“ and ”فَنُنْجِيَ“; it has been read ”فَنَجا مَن نَشاءُ“; and ʿĀṣim read ”فَنُجِّيَ مَن نَشاءُ“ with fatḥa of the yāʾ. As for whoever reads ”فَنُنْجِيَ“, it is as future, the nūn being the nūn of the imperfect — I mean the first nūn. Whoever reads ”فَنُجِّي“ with sukūn of the yāʾ elided the second nūn because of the meeting of the two nūns, as you say: "you tabayyanu this matter", meaning tatabayyanu, eliding because of the meeting of two tāʾs.
Whoever reads ”فَنَجا مَن نَشاءُ“ conjoins it to His saying "Our help came to them, so whom We willed was saved", in the form of the past verb. Whoever reads ”فَنُجِّيَ مَن نَشاءُ“ has it in the past sense, as a verb whose agent is not named [i.e. passive], and the position of ”مَن“ is nominative; it is known from the meaning that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saved them.
